name: Startplate
tagline: A prebuilt starter codebase for shipping a SaaS: auth, billing, orgs and email already wired up.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Scaffolding is the single thing coding agents are best at, so an agent will hand you a running Next.js app with auth, a database schema and a Stripe checkout flow in one sitting. The problem is that a boilerplate's value is not the first hour, it is the hundredth: webhook idempotency, subscription state drift, invite edge cases, email deliverability, session bugs on mobile Safari. A generated starter passes the demo and then eats a weekend of debugging the exact things a maintained template already fixed for everyone else. You also inherit the upgrade treadmill yourself, which is the part people quietly pay to outsource. Buildable, genuinely useful, but call it a weekend and not a one-shot.
coreLoopDIY: Generates your own opinionated Next.js plus Postgres starter with magic-link and OAuth auth, orgs and invites, Stripe subscriptions behind a signed webhook, and gated app routes.
requirements: A Stripe test account plus Stripe CLI for local webhooks
A GitHub OAuth app for social login
An email sending domain if you want magic links to reach real inboxes
whatYouLose: Someone else keeping the template current through Next.js, Auth.js and Stripe API churn
Edge cases already found by hundreds of other users: proration, failed payments, seat changes, refunds
Prebuilt polished UI blocks you would otherwise generate and then fight with
Docs and a support channel when the webhook silently stops updating subscription status
Reuse leverage: a paid template is used across projects, your generated one rots in one repo
moatNotes: The moat is accumulated bug fixes in billing and auth, not the file tree. That kind of moat erodes as agents get better at wiring Stripe.
whyPeopleStillPay: People pay for boilerplate to skip the boring, high-stakes plumbing exactly once and then reuse it forever, and because a template that hundreds of other developers are running has already had its billing and auth bugs found by someone else. The value is warranty and maintenance, not novelty. An agent-built starter is free and yours, which is great until Stripe changes an API or Auth.js ships a breaking major and nobody is on the hook but you.
notes: Generating a starter is easy, maintaining one is the actual product.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted SaaS starter template in this empty folder. One stack, no menus, no alternatives offered.

Stack: Next.js 15 with the App Router and TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Postgres 16 via docker-compose, Drizzle ORM with drizzle-kit migrations, Auth.js v5 using email magic links plus GitHub OAuth, Stripe Checkout for a single subscription product, Resend for transactional email with a console transport in dev.

In scope:
- Marketing landing page, pricing page, login page, and an authenticated dashboard shell
- Tables: users, sessions, organizations, memberships, subscriptions
- Organization switcher, invite by email, two roles: owner and member
- Stripe Checkout session route, billing portal redirect, and a signature-verified webhook handler that upserts subscription status idempotently
- Middleware gating every route under /app on both an active session and an active or trialing subscription
- Settings pages for profile, organization, and billing
- Transactional emails: magic link, invite, payment failed
- Seed script creating one org, one owner, one active fake subscription
- Vitest tests covering webhook idempotency (same event id twice changes nothing) and the gating middleware
- README with setup steps and a complete .env.example

Out of scope: admin panel, i18n, feature flags, analytics, telemetry of any kind, hosted dashboard. Do not phone home, do not add tracking scripts.

Rules:
- All secrets live in .env and are read through a single zod-validated env module. Never hardcode keys.
- Everything runs locally except outbound Stripe and OAuth calls. Document Stripe CLI webhook forwarding in the README.
- No paid or licensed UI kits. Plain Tailwind components under components/ui.
- pnpm only. Dev flow is: docker compose up, pnpm db:migrate, pnpm db:seed, pnpm dev.
- Stop only when pnpm test and pnpm build both pass, then print the dev URL and the seeded login email.
